cls: Endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA), dual ETA/ETB, for pulmonary arterial hypertension
pharm: An orally active, tissue-targeting dual antagonist of the endothelin-1 (ET-1) receptors ETA and ETB; by blocking the vasoconstrictive and proliferative effects of endothelin-1 it reduces pulmonary vascular resistance and pulmonary arterial pressure, slowing disease progression in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
quick: May be taken with or without food; swallow tablet whole
CONTRAINDICATED - boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity; exclude pregnancy first
Avoid breastfeeding during treatment; unknown if excreted in human milk
No dose adjustment for renal impairment; not recommended on dialysis (limited data)
Avoid in severe hepatic impairment; not recommended if ALT/AST >3x ULN at baseline
No specific interaction; avoid additional hepatotoxic insults
Pregnancy test (REMS), hemoglobin, LFTs, signs of pulmonary edema/fluid retention
summary: Macitentan is an orally active dual endothelin receptor antagonist (ETA and ETB) indicated for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to reduce the risk of disease progression and hospitalization for PAH. The dose is 10 mg once daily. It carries a BOXED WARNING for embryo-fetal toxicity: it can cause major birth defects and must not be used in pregnancy. Because of this risk, it is available only through a restricted Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program that requires exclusion of pregnancy before and during therapy, monthly pregnancy testing in females of reproductive potential, and use of acceptable contraception. Other important risks include hepatotoxicity, decreases in hemoglobin/anemia, and pulmonary edema in patients with veno-occlusive disease (PVOD).
indications: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to reduce the risk of disease progression and hospitalization for PAH; efficacy established in a long-term study with predominantly WHO functional class II-III patients, as monotherapy or in combination with other PAH therapies

dosage.n: Doses above 10 mg once daily have not been studied and are not recommended

dosage.d: 10 mg once daily only after a negative pregnancy test and with acceptable contraception
dosage.n: REMS requires monthly pregnancy testing during and 1 month after treatment

dosage.c: Severe hepatic impairment / elevated baseline aminotransferases
dosage.d: Avoid initiation if ALT/AST >3x ULN; generally avoid in severe hepatic impairment
dosage.n: Obtain liver enzymes before starting and as clinically indicated

admin: Take one 10 mg tablet once daily, at about the same time each day
May be taken with or without food
Swallow the tablet whole - do not split, crush, or chew
Prescribers, pharmacies, and patients must be enrolled in and comply with the REMS program before dispensing
Obtain a negative pregnancy test before starting and confirm acceptable contraception in females of reproductive potential
Measure liver enzymes and hemoglobin before initiating and periodically thereafter
moa: Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and its receptors ETA and ETB mediate vasoconstriction, fibrosis, proliferation, hypertrophy, and inflammation; the ET system is upregulated in pulmonary arterial hypertension and contributes to pathologic vascular remodeling and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Macitentan is a potent dual antagonist that binds both ETA and ETB receptors, displaying high affinity and sustained receptor occupancy in pulmonary vascular tissue. By blocking ET-1 binding it prevents the vasoconstrictive and pro-proliferative signaling that drives PAH progression. Its active metabolite (formed via oxidative depropylation, primarily by CYP3A4) is also pharmacologically active and contributes to the overall effect.

absolute: Pregnancy - can cause embryo-fetal harm (BOXED WARNING)
Known hypersensitivity to macitentan or any component
relative: Severe hepatic impairment or baseline aminotransferases >3x ULN
Suspected pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (risk of pulmonary edema)
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (reduced exposure) or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (increased exposure) - avoid concomitant use
monitor: Pregnancy status (monthly testing per REMS) in females of reproductive potential
Liver aminotransferases (ALT/AST) before and during treatment as clinically indicated
Signs of pulmonary edema and fluid retention/edema

preg: BOXED WARNING - EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY: Macitentan may cause fetal harm when administered during pregnancy and is contraindicated in females who are pregnant. In animals, endothelin receptor antagonists, including macitentan, produced teratogenic effects including malformations of the head, mouth, face, and large blood vessels. Because of the risk of birth defects, macitentan is available only through the restricted OPSUMIT REMS program. Females of reproductive potential must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, must use acceptable methods of contraception during and for 1 month after treatment, and must have monthly pregnancy tests during therapy. If pregnancy occurs, stop the drug immediately.
lact: There is no information on the presence of macitentan in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production. Macitentan and its metabolite were present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with macitentan.
renal: No clinically relevant change in exposure was observed in patients with renal impairment, and no dose adjustment is required for renal impairment. Macitentan has not been studied in patients on dialysis; it is highly protein bound and not expected to be dialyzable. Use with caution and is generally not recommended in dialysis patients due to limited data.
hepatic: Macitentan exposure is somewhat decreased in hepatic impairment, but the active metabolite changes are not clinically significant; no dose adjustment is required for mild or moderate hepatic impairment. It has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment and should generally be avoided. Do not initiate in patients with baseline ALT or AST greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal. Endothelin receptor antagonists as a class have been associated with elevations of aminotransferases and rare cases of hepatic injury; measure liver enzymes before treatment and repeat during therapy as clinically indicated.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) - significantly reduce macitentan exposure and may decrease efficacy; avoid concomitant use
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - increase macitentan exposure (approximately doubled); avoid concomitant use
moderate: Moderate dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, amiodarone) - may increase exposure; use with caution
Other PAH therapies (PDE-5 inhibitors, prostacyclins) - commonly combined; monitor blood pressure and fluid status
minor: Warfarin - no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction observed
Sildenafil - no clinically significant change in exposure of either drug
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not meaningfully affect exposure.
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacokinetic interaction with alcohol; avoid additional hepatotoxic exposures given the risk of aminotransferase elevations.
interactions.diagnostics: Decreases in hemoglobin/hematocrit may be seen on complete blood counts; aminotransferases (ALT/AST) may rise. Monitor hemoglobin and liver enzymes.

serious: Marked decrease in hemoglobin / anemia requiring transfusion
Pulmonary edema in patients with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD)
Decreased sperm count (potential effect on fertility, as with other ERAs)
emergency: Signs of acute pulmonary edema (worsening dyspnea, hypoxia) suggesting PVOD
Signs of liver injury (jaundice, dark urine, right upper quadrant pain, nausea, fatigue)

monitoring: Pregnancy testing before initiation and monthly during treatment per the REMS program (females of reproductive potential)
Hemoglobin/hematocrit before initiation and periodically during treatment
Liver aminotransferases (ALT/AST) before initiation and during treatment as clinically indicated
Signs and symptoms of pulmonary edema (consider PVOD; discontinue if confirmed)
Fluid retention and peripheral edema; assess for underlying heart failure
Clinical response and PAH disease progression
counsel: This medicine can cause severe birth defects - you must not be pregnant while taking it
If you can become pregnant, you must use reliable birth control and have a pregnancy test before starting and every month during treatment
You can only get this medicine through a special program (REMS); follow all its requirements
Tell your doctor right away if you think you may be pregnant or miss a period - stop the medicine and call immediately
Take one tablet once daily, with or without food, swallowed whole
Report unusual tiredness, pale skin, or shortness of breath, which may signal low blood counts
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, nausea, or right-sided belly pain, which may signal liver problems
Tell your doctor about swelling in the legs or sudden worsening of breathing
pk: Steady state reached within about 3 days of once-daily dosing
Plasma Tmax approximately 8 hours after oral administration
Approximately 16 hours (macitentan); active metabolite approximately 48 hours
Once-daily dosing maintained by long receptor occupancy and active metabolite
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); keep in original container, protect from moisture
pearls: BOXED WARNING for embryo-fetal toxicity - REMS program with monthly pregnancy testing and mandatory contraception in females of reproductive potential
Once-daily 10 mg dosing; doses above 10 mg are not more effective and not recommended
Has an active metabolite with a long half-life contributing to sustained effect
Check hemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline and periodically; anemia and aminotransferase elevations are class effects of endothelin receptor antagonists
Do not start if ALT/AST >3x ULN; avoid in severe hepatic impairment
If pulmonary edema develops, consider pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and discontinue if confirmed
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one. If you miss several days, contact your healthcare provider before restarting.
overdose: Macitentan has been administered as a single dose up to 600 mg in healthy subjects, with adverse events of headache, nausea, and vomiting. In the event of overdose, standard supportive measures should be undertaken as required. Because macitentan is highly protein bound, dialysis is unlikely to be effective. There is no specific antidote.
